links.outcome: AUC of retina foundation model versus supervised deep-learning models on same test data
links.effect: Similar ocular disease AUCs with full datasets (traditional 0.914-0.965 vs RETFound 0.938-0.966); RETFound outperformed on systemic disease and on glaucoma/DR with small fine-tuning sets.
links.quote: Under this specific study design, the performance of traditional deep-learning models is similar to that of RETFound for ocular disease detection when fine-tuned on large datasets.

links.outcome: Performance drop from internal to external test datasets
links.effect: RETFound glaucoma AUC after 400 images was 0.908 on internal SEED, versus 0.835 on ODIR-5K and 0.779 on PAPILA, but 0.990 on GAMMA; systemic hypertension AUC about 0.62 on UKBB versus 0.705 internally.
links.quote: As an example for glaucoma detection, after fine-tuning on 400 images, RETFound had an AUC of 0·908 (95% CI 0·888-0·928) when tested on the internal SEED dataset and, for the external datasets, AUCs of 0·835 (0·816-0·855) when tested on ODIR-5K, 0·779 (0·731-0·826) on PAPILA, and 0·990 (0·974-1·000) on GAMMA, performing significantly better than ResNet50 (SEED p=0·0001; ODIR-5k p<0·0001; PAPILA p=0·0032; and GAMMA p=0·0010).

unlisted_practices: Label-efficient fine-tuning of foundation models on small datasets

screen.reason: The study is an empirical benchmark comparing the label efficiency and performance of a retinal foundation model (RETFound) against standard deep learning architectures across multiple disease detection tasks without testing clinical deployment practices or guardrails.
